15748               	;
15749               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
15750               	; 	'
15751               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
15752               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
15753               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
15754               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
15755               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
15756               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
15757               	; 	'
15758               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
15759               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
15760               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
15761               	; 	'
15762               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
15763               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
15764               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
15765               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
15766               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
15767               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
15768               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
15769               	; 	'
15770               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
15771               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
15772               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
15773               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
15774               	; 	'
15775               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
15776               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
15777               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
15778               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
15779               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
15780               	; 	'
15781               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
15782               	; 	' did not finish.
15783               	; pause_beat:
15784               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

16075               	;
16076               	; 	' the jump sweep: divisor falling = pitch rising
16077               	; 	' THE JUMP IS A WARBLE, NOT A SWEEP -- testsounds variant A, measured off
16078               	; 	' the 2600 at about 415 Hz alternating with 188 for roughly 280 ms.
16079               	; 	'
16080               	; 	' It used to be a rising sweep, 500 down to 120 in steps of 40. That was
16081               	; 	' invented rather than measured, and it had the wrong SHAPE: a sweep reads
16082               	; 	' as something departing, which is a fine idea and is not what the original
16083               	; 	' does. Eight ticks alternating is four cycles of warble, which is what the

16147               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
16148               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
16149               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
16150               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
16151               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
16152               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
16153               	;
16154               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
16155               	; 	'
16156               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
16157               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
16158               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
16159               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
16160               	; 	'
16161               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
16162               	; 	'
16163               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
16164               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
16165               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
16166               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
16167               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
16168               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
16169               	; 	'
16170               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
16171               	; 	'
16172               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
16173               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
16174               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
16175               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
16176               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
16177               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
16178               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
16179               	; 	'
16180               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
16181               	; 	'
16182               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
16183               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
16184               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
16185               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
16186               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
16187               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
16188               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
16189               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
16190               	; 	'
16191               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
16192               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
16193               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
16194               	; 	'
16195               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench

16198               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
16199               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
16200               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.

16205               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
16206               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to

16208               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of

16419               	;
16420               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
16421               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
16422               	; 	'
16423               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
16424               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
16425               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
16426               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
16427               	; 	'
16428               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
16429               	; 	'
16430               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
16431               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
16432               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
16433               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
16434               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
16435               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
16436               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
16437               	; 	'
16438               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
16439               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
16440               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
16441               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
16442               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
16443               	; 	'
16444               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
16445               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
16446               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
16447               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
16448               	; 	#if TI994A
16449               	; 	BANK 2
16450      01EC     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

16588               	;
16589               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($B4 = black ink on dark blue).
16590               	; 	'
16591               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
16592               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
16593               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
16594               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
16595               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
16596               	; 	'
16597               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
16598               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
16599               	;
16600               	; font_col:
16601               cvb_FONT_COL

16924               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY LIST, for the same reason as the font: walked
16925               	; 	' once by title_draw, at boot and on a return to the title, and never
16926               	; 	' during play. title_draw selects bank 2 around its walk.
16927               	; 	'
16928               	; 	' ITS MESSAGE BOXES DID NOT COME WITH IT. They are the same format and
16929               	; 	' were in the same generated file, which is what made this worth doing
16930               	; 	' carefully: they are walked when a ROUND ENDS, mid-game, so on bank 2
16931               	; 	' they would have returned bytes from the wrong page at the moment a life
16932               	; 	' is lost -- and with no error at build or run time. gentitle.py now
16933               	; 	' writes them to title.bas below, which stays in bank 1.
16934               	; 	INCLUDE "titledl.bas"
16935               	; 	' ==================================================
16936               	; 	' THE TITLE SCREEN, AS A DISPLAY LIST
16937               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py -- do not edit here.
16938               	; 	'
16939               	; 	' row, col, length, then `length` bytes; 255 ends.
16940               	; 	' Walked by title_draw only.
16941               	; 	'
16942               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2, with the fonts, because it is read ONCE
16943               	; 	' -- at boot and on a return to the title. title_draw
16944               	; 	' selects bank 2 around its walk and restores bank 1.
16945               	; 	' The message boxes in title.bas are the same format and
16946               	; 	' CANNOT come with it: they are read when a round ends.
16947               	; 	' ==================================================
16948               	;
16949               	; title_tbl:

17177               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
17178               	; 	'
17179               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
17180               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
17181               	; 	' being small sprites.
17182               	; 	'
17183               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
17184               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
17185               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
17186               	; 	'
17187               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
17188               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
17189               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
17190               	;
17191               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/the four merged run bodies/duck hat/face/body, then the same LEFT (+36). The run bodies carry tunic AND legs, so a frame is one sprite. Patterns 0..68

18432               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
18433               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
18434               	; 	'
18435               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
18436               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
18437               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
18438               	; 	'
18439               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
18440               	; 	' blit is
18441               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
18442               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
18443               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
18444               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
18445               	; 	'
18446               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
18447               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
18448               	; 	'
18449               	; 	' template ids:
18450               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
18451               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
18452               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
18453               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
18454               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
18455               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
18456               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
18457               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
18458               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
18459               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
18460               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
18461               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
18462               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
18463               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
18464               	; 	'   14 T_END_E

19082               	;
19083               	; 	' THE SKYLINE'S LAST BAND WITHOUT ITS YELLOW, high nibble ink, low nibble
19084               	; 	' paper, one byte a scan line -- the same shape genart emits into
19085               	; 	' store_col. SKY2 is white-on-9 throughout instead of turning to paper 10
19086               	; 	' at row 4; BLDGL holds its blue one row longer and then meets its own
19087               	; 	' grey wall. Both are the generated bytes with 10 replaced by 9 and
19088               	; 	' nothing else changed. See setup_rest.
19089               	; #if NES
19090               	; nes_sky2c:
19091               	; 	DATA BYTE $F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9
19092               	; nes_bldlc:
19093               	; 	DATA BYTE $B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$BE,$BE,$BE
19094               	; #endif
19095               	;
19096               	; 	' THE IN-GAME FONT'S COLOUR, one byte a scan line and eight a character for
19097               	; 	' all 59 of them. $B4 is light yellow on dark blue -- ink index 3, paper index 1 --
19098               	; 	' and which colours those are is then the attribute table's business, per
19099               	; 	' region: dark blue behind the HUD, the store's green behind a message box.
19100               	; 	'
19101               	; 	' 472 bytes of one repeated value. That reads like waste and is the cheap
19102               	; 	' option: ROM is three budgets here and this is not the scarce one, while
19103               	; 	' the alternative is a second font (impossible -- only eleven free codes)
19104               	; 	' or a new uploader parameter (no RAM -- two bytes left).
19105               	; #if NES
19106               	; nes_fcol:
19107               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
19108               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
19109               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
19110               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
19111               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
19112               	; 	DATA BYTE $B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4,$B4
